_comment: W64-A7 ORCHESTRATOR ACTION -- APPEND this row to the EXISTING
PER_FN_TEXT_MOVES['recon/syslib/psx/libpad/MCXMAIN.c']['_padIntRecvHdr'] list,
AFTER the already-wired w62 copy+slot row (order matters: the anchors below
match the region AFTER that row has run).  Do NOT create a second dict key
(12F duplicate-key shadowing).
WHAT IT FIXES: _padIntRecvHdr gates PASS 35/35 today, but brdist reports two
BRANCH-OFFSET divergences -- rows (1, 6, 7) and (2, 4, 5), i.e. our `beq` and
`beqz` both target the merge label ONE INSTRUCTION EARLIER than retail's.  The
cause is label PLACEMENT, not code: cc1 emits `$L19:` BEFORE the merge-point
`addu $2,$3,$0`, so our two early exits land on the copy; retail's label sits
AFTER it (its `.L8010C304` is the `lw $ra`), so retail's branches skip the copy
-- which is legal there because the FIRST branch's delay slot already performed
it.  Semantically identical, but two different branch WORDS: the 04Q gate blind
spot in its pure form, on a fn the gate calls PASS.
The row MOVES THE LABEL LINE past the copy (15-series: labels ARE movable
lines).  After it, $L19 and $L21 coincide and both branches encode retail's
offsets.
MEASURED (scratchpad/w64a7/tmprobe.py + tmbrdist.py, build.py never edited,
each run twice, identical):
WITHOUT: _padIntRecvHdr PASS 35/35, brdist 2 offset diffs [(1,6,7),(2,4,5)]
WITH:    _padIntRecvHdr PASS 35/35, brdist 0 offset diffs
whole TU WITH the row: _padIntInit PASS 18 | _padIntQuery PASS 54 |
_padIntRecvId PASS 48 | _padIntRecvHdr PASS 35 |
_padIntRecvData PASS 223   => 5/5, zero regressions.
ANCHOR SAFETY: `take` is the label line pinned by a lookahead on the exact
three following lines (copy, label, `lw $31,`), which occurs once in the fn;
`after` is the copy line pinned by a lookahead on (label, `lw $31,`), also
unique.  Both are $L-number agnostic (a TU reorder renumbers every $L).
FOLLOW-UP, SAME FAMILY, NOT SOLVED: _padIntRecvData also gates PASS 223/223
with ONE brdist offset row (13, 34, 35) -- its `beqz $v0` targets the
merge-point `addu $4,$17,$0` (obj 0x4a4) where retail targets the following
`lui` (0x4a8).  Same label-placement question, a different label; not probed.
